newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Apr diesel trades at $26.80/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Apr diesel trades at $26.80/bbl.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady at late afternoon in uninspired trading as players brushed off the weaker crude market and looked to sustained buying from a local trader to support prices, industry sources said.
"The market is holding its own. Everyone expects Hin Leong to continue buying for another few days," one trader said.
April gas oil was last quoted up five cents from Thursday at $26.75/$26.85 per barrel, brokers said. They said April traded earlier in the day at $26.80.
May was last quoted at $25.25/$25.35 per barrel, also up five cents, with a deal seen earlier at $25.30.
The April/May time spread widened to $1.40/$1.50 per barrel from below $1.00 early week as a result of the strong prompt demand, they said.
Traders said the steep backwardation was a clear reflection of the high premiums paid by traders for prompt cargoes.
On Thursday, a 150,000-barrel cargo loading April 18-22 traded at $27.50 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, about 70 cents above the value for balance April swaps.
The trader who bought the cargo was also responsible for buying up around seven million barrels of gas oil in March.
The same trader also bought another 150,000-barrel lot at $26.80 for April 29-May loading, again reflecting the steeply backwardated market.
The backwardation has sent middle distillate stocks to one of their lowest levels in years at 4.953 million barrels for the week ending April 2, according to the Trade Development Board.
Overnight, May Brent crude lost 33 cents to close at $18.27 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange, on top of the 60 cents it lost on Wednesday and last traded up two cents at $18.20.
The April jet fuel/gas oil regrade was quoted unchanged at -90/-70 cents, brokers said.
Fuel oil swaps edged down following the weaker crude with April last quoted at $98.00/$99.00, down about 50 cents from Thursday.
